purpose: Non-admission original-provider discovery of five distinct 2026 critical-infrastructure, DOI wildfire, hydrodynamic, UK urban flood monitoring and USDA community wildfire benchmark products. No source admission, data retrieval or permission inferred.

entries.name: Global Exposure and Risk Database: multi-hazard critical infrastructure v1.0.0
entries.provider: Nirandjan and Koks / Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Oxford / Zenodo
entries.spatial_scope: Global GADM Admin-2 region summaries across energy, transport, telecom, waste, water, education and healthcare; geography follows source GADM boundaries
entries.temporal_scope: Zenodo version 1.0.0, released 2026-09-14; hazard and exposure input vintages differ and must be recovered from methodology before comparisons
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Eight main XLSX workbooks: global_infra_risk plus seven sector exposure summaries; additional design-standard sensitivity ZIP; admin-2 risk quantiles min/Q1/Q2/Q3/max and return-period suffixes for lengths (km), areas (m2), and counts
entries.note: Provider states modeled multi-hazard risk estimates and exposure summaries; NOT observed insured losses, building-level geocoordinates, independent event footprints or insurer TIV. Baseline design standard explicitly assumes 1-in-10-year protection for floods, tropical cyclones and landslides, and 1-in-475-year protection for earthquakes; published sensitivity scenarios vary design standards (none, 10, 50, 100, 150, 475, 975-year). Treat these design standards, per-hazard return periods, modeled expected annual damage quantiles and multi-hazard sums as distinct from event-level joint exceedance or observed insurer payouts. Trace original vulnerability curves and asset layers to Nirandjan's already registered physical vulnerability and infrastructure products before claiming independent validation. Freeze source GADM version and publication files. Published MD5 labels are provider metadata, not our SHA-256 byte receipts. Exact dataset license and all upstream reuse rights unreviewed; no file bytes acquired.

entries.name: DOI Wildland Fire Service wildfire risk map 2026
entries.provider: US Geological Survey / US Department of the Interior / US Wildland Fire Service
entries.spatial_scope: Conterminous United States, Alaska and Hawaii in separate, regionally projected raster products
entries.temporal_scope: USGS data release published 2026-11-04; source Wildfire Hazard Potential references 2023 WHP, 2020 LANDFIRE-based fuels and earlier upstream data
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Regional risk and risk-classification raster layers plus life, property and infrastructure valuation proxies, 2400-m buffered combinations, wilderness mask, separate metadata and data_dictionary.csv
entries.note: USGS DOI release DOI 10.5066/P14VT8QI labels the work CC0 1.0, but maintain rights not_reviewed until checking exact asset metadata and source-derived layers. Source explicitly limits intended interpretation to DOI responsibilities; not a comprehensive wildfire risk assessment for all non-DOI properties, not annual burn probability, not asset replacement cost and not insured loss. WHP uses existing LANDFIRE and FSIM inputs; not independent of other US wildfire hazard layers. Do not turn categorical WHP into an event set or treat 2400-m buffers as actual fire perimeters.

entries.name: Observed inundation and hydrodynamic simulation data
entries.provider: Rusjan and Donevska (dataset); Mikoš (paper coauthor) / University of Ljubljana / Zenodo
entries.spatial_scope: Lower Vipava River valley, western Slovenia: last 21 km of the river in Slovenia before it enters Italy; original GeoTIFF grid/CRS/vertical datum remain to be checked
entries.temporal_scope: Zenodo record 22275184 released in 2026; the linked 2026 NHESS article identifies the observed flood extent as September 2010; modeled Q10/Q100/Q500 are design return-period scenarios, not observation dates
entries.resolution_or_granularity: Observed inundation extent archive plus GeoTIFF hydrodynamic simulations for Q10, Q100, Q500 and multiple channel/floodplain/uncertainty configurations
entries.note: The peer-reviewed source paper (Rusjan, Donevska and Mikoš, NHESS 26, 5647–5665, 2026; DOI 10.5194/nhess-26-5647-2026) locates the study on the lower Vipava, and identifies the mapped historical inundation as the September 2010 flood. This empirical event must remain separate from hydrodynamic Q10/Q100/Q500 and their 10/90 confidence/sensitivity ensembles; scenario exceedance maps are not independently observed claim events or annual occurrence sequences. Zenodo displays CC BY 4.0 for this record, but exact source and raster reuse rights and upstream dependencies still require a dataset-level review. Verify original GeoTIFF units, CRS, NoData, terrain/vertical datum, flood-event mask and model ensemble settings before any hazard validation. No source bytes fetched, no insurance losses inferred, no scientific admission.

entries.name: Blue Heart high-density urban hydrometric and sewer monitoring dataset
entries.provider: Sweetapple, Illingworth and Melville-Shreeve / University of Exeter / East Sussex County Council / Zenodo
entries.spatial_scope: 78 km2 urban catchment in East Sussex, UK, including rainfall, rivers, groundwater, road gullies and in-sewer gauges
entries.temporal_scope: Zenodo record 20699635, project release v1.0 in 2026; individual instrument sampling dates and completeness must be verified from index/README
entries.resolution_or_granularity: 497 sensor locations with multiple telemetry datasets, catchment and network shapefiles; index_telemetry_data.csv and original README are metadata-first review targets
entries.note: Provider dataset lists 497 gauges over 78 km2 and separate archives including 331-MB catchment geometry, 231-MB sewer telemetry and small index file. Publication page has an unpopulated Rights/License display as accessed at this review, so the general Zenodo default cannot be taken as evidence of this exact record's licence. Linked ESSD preprint DOI 10.5194/essd-2026-569 and Blue Heart data-processing scripts DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21390823 are useful methodology/software references, not new independent gauge data; commercial use, derivative publication and exact observation rights remain unknown. First inspect versioned metadata and README, then timestamps/timezones, rainfall units and gauge quality flags. A rain or water-level observation is not a flood polygon, sewer loss, insured claim, or independent exposure inventory. Do not ingest sensor or infrastructure locations into public Git.

entries.name: Wildfire Risk to Communities all-lands and populated-area GIS layers
entries.provider: US Department of Agriculture / US Forest Service
entries.spatial_scope: United States nationally consistent, downloadable state GIS rasters and community/county/tribal summaries; check coverage and edition by jurisdiction
entries.temporal_scope: USDA Forest Service Research Data Archive all-lands 2nd edition reference RDS-2020-0016-2 (2024); website dashboard updated through April 2026 independently of GIS release
entries.resolution_or_granularity: GIS rasters including annual burn probability, conditional flame length, risk to potential structures and building/housing summaries; several building grids described as 30-meter pixels
entries.note: Original USDA 2024 methodology states FSim annual burn probability was simulated on an approximately 270-m grid and upsampled to 30-m LANDFIRE resolution; upsampling does not create independent 30-m burn-probability information. Annual burn probability is a distinct probability variable; conditional flame length and risk-to-home indices are not interchangeable and none is an insurer payout. The public ArcGIS ImageServer warns its pixel values may differ from original raster due to service rendering requirements: use version-pinned original Research Data Archive rasters, not ImageServer pixel values, for quantitative comparisons. Published risk is generalized and not parcel-level/home-specific. Underlying LANDFIRE/FSIM, FEMA USA Structures, Census and related sources may overlap DOI USWFS and existing OpenCatastrophe wildfire candidates; do not use the two products as independent holdouts by default. Separate 2024 versioned GIS from 2026 website content, check raster dates, projection, NoData, license and training inputs before use. No source bytes acquired.
